references.text: Moses uses similar language in his intercession after the golden calf incident, reminding God that Israel is His people whom He brought out of Egypt with great power.
Describes Israel as God's inheritance whom He brought out of Egypt, the iron furnace.
Refers to God's mighty acts when He took Israel out of Egypt with a stretched-out arm.
Reminds of God's great power and stretched-out arm that brought Israel out of Egypt.
Describes how the Lord brought Israel out of Egypt with a strong hand and a stretched-out arm.
Solomon's prayer at the temple dedication uses the same expression about Israel as God's inheritance, brought out of Egypt.
Nehemiah's prayer uses similar language about Israel as God's people, redeemed with great power and a strong hand.
Jeremiah refers to the deliverance from Egypt with signs and wonders, with a strong hand and a stretched-out arm.
Paul speaks of how God brought His people out of Egypt with an uplifted arm.
